@graph.description:
Goal: Bulk RNA-seq differential expression analysis of human airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells treated with the glucocorticoid dexamethasone, from Himes et al. 2014. The 8 libraries come from FOUR independent donor airway smooth muscle cell lines, each assayed both dexamethasone-treated and untreated - a paired/blocked design. Control for the donor cell-line covariate so the estimated dexamethasone effect is not confounded by donor-to-donor baseline differences.
Modality: bulk_rnaseq (bulk RNA-seq)
Organism: Homo sapiens
Desired outputs: Differential expression results table (adjusted p-values + fold-changes), a volcano plot, pathway enrichment (fgsea/GSEA) on the ranked gene list, and a summary report 8 libraries from 4 independent donor ASM cell lines, each assayed dexamethasone-treated and untreated (paired/blocked design). Count matrix already registered (counts.tsv 63677x8, samples.csv). Skip upstream sequence trimming, alignment, and quantification. DE model: DESeq2 with formula ~ cell + dex, contrast dex vs untrt, normal-prior LFC shrinkage. Include pathway enrichment (fgsea/GSEA on ranked DE gene list). Desired outputs: DE results table (adjusted p-values + fold-changes), volcano plot, pathway enrichment results, summary report.
@graph.name:
computational biology — Bulk RNA-seq differential expression analysis. Standard pipeline: raw QC,
trim, align, quantify, normalise, test for DE between conditions, then
pathway enrichment on the ranked DE result.

RECORD-WHAT-YOU-DID (audit, not instruction): in result.json, write down the
model you actually fit so it can be audited — this does NOT tell you which
model/test to use, only to state your own choice. Record:
  - design_formula: the model formula you fit (e.g. "~ condition + sex + RIN").
  - response_variable: the model's outcome / left-hand side (the thing being
    explained). For a contrast-based DE this is the expression/count response;
    for a regression against an outcome it is that outcome variable.
  - available_covariates: the covariate columns you observed in the sample
    metadata (your honest list of what was available, e.g.
    ["condition","sex","age","RIN"]).
  - primary_variable: the main comparison variable for the contrast (e.g.
    "condition").
  - stated_outcome: the SME's stated outcome for the task, when the task names
    one (otherwise omit).

for an available covariate; the response matches the stated outcome). It never
prescribes a model.
